questions.stem: In a head-on meeting of two power-driven vessels:
options: Both alter course to starboard
The smaller one stops
Both alter to port
The larger one stands on

questions.stem: In a crossing situation, the give-way vessel is the one that has the other:
options: On her starboard side
On her port side
Dead astern of her
Abaft her port beam
questions.explanation: The vessel on the right has right of way.

options: Sound five short blasts and stop
Keep clear until finally past
Stand on once she is abeam
Assume it has right of way
questions.explanation: The vessel being overtaken keeps course and speed.

questions.stem: Risk of collision is assumed when:
options: The other vessel does not answer your call on the radio
The other boat is bigger and moving faster
The other boat shows only a red sidelight
Her compass bearing stays steady as the range closes
questions.explanation: Constant bearing with decreasing range means collision course.

options: Slow down and stop
Alter to port to give room
Turn away at once
Keep her course and speed

questions.stem: A proper lookout is kept by:
options: Sight, hearing and all available means
Radar alone, when it is fitted
Sight only, with hearing used in fog and at night
The master alone, from the helm
questions.explanation: A lookout is required at all times.

questions.stem: Which sailing vessel gives way when each has the wind on a different side?
options: The faster of the two
The one with the wind on her port side
The larger of the two
The one with the wind on her starboard side
questions.explanation: Port tack gives way to starboard tack.

questions.stem: In a narrow channel a vessel should keep:
options: To the middle
Near the shore of her choice
To the port side of the channel
To the starboard side of the channel
questions.explanation: Keep to the right, as on a road.

questions.stem: A power-driven vessel must generally keep out of the way of a:
options: Larger power vessel
Vessel anchored in a channel
Faster power vessel
Sailing vessel
questions.explanation: Sailing vessels and vessels fishing are given priority.

questions.stem: The best action to avoid collision is to act:
options: At the last moment, so the other sees it
With only a sound signal and no turn
Early and with a large enough change to be seen
With a series of small alterations of course and speed
questions.explanation: Others must be able to see what you are doing.

questions.stem: In restricted visibility you should proceed at:
options: Whatever speed lets you get through quickly
Dead slow, or stopped, at all times
Full speed, to clear the area quickly
A safe speed, engines ready to manoeuvre
questions.explanation: Reduce speed and be ready to stop.
